heard: A monster solar storm missed, erasing our modern world by nine days. In July 2012, the sun launched a massive eruption matching the strongest storm ever recorded. This blast traveled over 2,000 kilometers per second, four times faster than a typical storm. It achieved this record speed because another eruption four days earlier had cleared its cosmic path. A direct hit would have crippled global power grids and water pumps, costing over $2 trillion. Instead, NASA's STEREOAS spacecraft took the hit and survived to show us what we missed. Physicist Pete Riley calculated a 12% chance a similar storm strikes Earth every decade. We survived only because the erupting region of the sun was no longer pointed directly at us. You
